text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright expected to visit Middle East in near future after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat meet.
- More rioting in Hebron, Bethlehem.
- 84-year-old woman in Ashdod obtains driver's license on 35th try!
- Bad real-estate loans damage Discount Bank profits. Net profits dropped 85 percent in fourth quarter from same period in previous year.
- Etgar Fund negotiating to buy controlling interest in Shemen Industries, a subsidiary of Koor Industries, says a source close to the company.
- Israel Chemicals net sharply up in 1996.
GLOBES
- Israel's Egged bus cooperative will begin structural changes this year ahead of privatisation in 1998.
- Israel asks the United States for $50-70 million to finance Arrow anti-missile missile project.
HAARETZ

- Suspicion: Israeli Arabs helped terrorist who carried out Tel Aviv cafe attack. Security forces check whether he brought explosive material with him from village, or got it in Greater Tel Aviv area.
- Mother of the suicide bomber: He slept at home the night before the attack.
- Two schools in Jerusalem cancel visits to Masada. High school headmaster: Defenders of Masada were murderers.
- Children of settlers in Hebron attack Arabs with teargas their parents supply them.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Suspicion: The suicide terrorist was helped by Israeli Arabs. Palestinian security forces sever contact with Shin Bet and Israeli army.
- Labour Minister Eli Yishai: Despite the terror -- the number of workers from the West Bank and Gaza must be increased.

- When Bar-On affair ends, Netanyahu expected to give final OK for unity government with Shimon Peres as finance minister, Ehud Barak as defence minister, Rafael Eitan as public security minister and Yitzhak Mordechai in some senior economic position.
MAARIV
- Palestinian security chiefs: We'll not make the effort to stop suicide attackers. Israel's President Ezer Weizman acts to set up Netanyahu-Arafat meeting.
- Jibril Rajoub, Palestinian preventive security chief for the West Bank, tells Maariv: "Listen to me well -- at the meeting on March 9 no one gave a green light for attacks".
- Great concern: Security situation will revive crisis in tourism sector.
